chunks: And from him (Al-Hamadani) from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah and Muhammad ibn Sahl from his father from his elders from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and a group of our companions who narrated from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) that they said:

"When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered the state of Ihram, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said to him: 'Order your companions to perform Al-Ajj and Al-Thaj.' Al-Ajj is raising the voice, and Al-Thaj is slaughtering the camels."
They (the Imams) said: "Jabir ibn Abdullah said: 'We did not walk through Al-Rawha' until our voices became hoarse (from loud recitation).'
And there is no requirement for women to be loud (profoundly) in the Talbiyah. This was narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between men and women regarding loudness in Talbiyah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of *Ihjar* (raising the voice) in Talbiyah, linking the Prophet’s command via Gabriel to the physical exertion of Jabir ibn Abdullah, thereby validating the practice as a manifestation of spiritual intensity. It further clarifies the juristic distinction between men and women, noting that while men are encouraged to be loud, women are exempt from this requirement, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on gender-specific ritual nuances during Hajj.
